title: Think Less, Act Early: Reinforced Latent Reasoning with Early Exit in Vision-Language-Action Models
one_liner: Replace long written reasoning with a hidden state sequence and stop early when the state is already confident enough to act.
lead: Vision-language-action models often reason by writing many intermediate text steps before choosing an action. That can be slow, and each extra step creates another chance to drift off course. This paper keeps the reasoning inside a hidden state sequence instead of forcing it into text, trains that sequence with task-level reward so that useful internal paths are favored, and adds an early-stop rule so the model can act as soon as the state looks confident enough.

problem.h2: Why explicit long-form reasoning can slow embodied control
paras: A vision-language-action model must turn camera input and instructions into actions. One common strategy is to write many intermediate reasoning steps in text before acting. That can help, but it also raises cost because every extra written step takes time and can introduce a fresh mistake.

The problem becomes sharper in long tasks. If an early written step drifts away from the useful plan, later steps inherit that drift. So the model needs a way to think through the task without paying for long visible reasoning, because a shorter internal path may already support a good action.

callout.html: Keep reasoning in hidden states and stop when confidence is high enough, because acting early avoids unnecessary computation and reduces opportunities for step-by-step drift.

panels.title: 1. Old route writes many steps

panels.caption: Written reasoning is costly because every visible step takes extra time.

panels.title: 2. New route keeps a hidden state path
panels.caption: The model updates an internal path without writing it out, because action does not require visible prose.

panels.title: 3. Reward favors cleaner internal paths
panels.caption: Task reward promotes useful internal states because successful action raises the score.

panels.title: 4. Confidence can trigger early stop
panels.caption: The model can stop thinking and act because more internal steps are no longer paying off.

panels.title: 5. Faster acting with steadier control
panels.caption: Shorter internal paths help when they preserve good decisions because they cut delay and drift.

steps.text: Start from the current observation and task request so that the action depends on the scene and goal together.

steps.b: Roll the hidden reasoning state forward
steps.text: Update an internal state sequence instead of writing visible reasoning, because the model can plan without producing extra text.
Use reinforcement learning to favor internal paths that lead to successful actions so that useful state progress is reinforced.
Check whether the current state already supports a stable action because more reasoning is only worth the cost when it changes the decision.
Act immediately when confidence is high, or keep updating the state when uncertainty remains.

paras: The paper changes the reasoning object from visible text steps to a hidden state trajectory whose length can vary from one decision to the next.
object.object: hidden reasoning trajectory with learned stopping

hidden.name: action confidence along the hidden reasoning path
paras: The important hidden quantity is action confidence at each internal step. Confidence matters because the model should stop only when the current state already supports a good action. If the state is still unstable, early stopping would lock in a weak decision.

The method estimates this confidence from the current hidden state and uses it to decide whether another reasoning step is worth the extra cost. That balance matters because the best number of internal steps changes from one scene to another.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark internal states where acting now is more likely to preserve strong behavior.

reads.html: The model watches how sure it is after each internal step and acts when that certainty is high enough, because extra thinking is only useful when it still changes the answer.
The framework learns a confidence-guided stopping policy over hidden reasoning states so that computation is spent only where it improves action quality.

mechanism.h2: Why hidden reasoning plus early stop helps
paras: Keeping reasoning inside hidden states removes the need to spell out every intermediate thought. That lowers answering time because visible text generation is skipped. It also avoids some error accumulation because a long written chain can introduce mistakes that later steps then copy.

The reward-driven training matters because not every hidden path is useful. By rewarding paths that lead to successful actions, the method shapes the internal updates toward states that support good control. Early stopping then uses the confidence estimate to quit when more updates are unlikely to help, because easy cases often reach a stable decision sooner while hard ones still need extra internal processing.

stages.s: faster stable control because short paths are enough on easy cases

math.h2: Stop when confidence passes the threshold
math.words: At each internal step, compare the action confidence to a stopping threshold. If confidence is high enough, act; otherwise keep updating the hidden state.
symbols: the decision to end reasoning at step t
the model's confidence in the current action at internal step t
the stopping threshold that determines whether more reasoning is needed

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: After step 1, confidence is 0.55, so the model continues.
After step 2, confidence is 0.74, so it still continues.
After step 3, confidence is 0.86, so it stops and acts.
If another scene reaches 0.82 at step 1, the model can act immediately because extra internal steps are not needed.

math.note: The paper's full training rule is more detailed, but this threshold view captures the main operational idea: spend internal computation only until the state is good enough to act.

charts.title: Always write full reasoning
charts.note: Full written reasoning is slow and can drift because every extra visible step creates more opportunities for mistakes.

charts.title: AVA-VLA
charts.note: The new design acts sooner without losing control because it keeps useful reasoning internal and stops early on easier cases.

items.html: If the model feels sure too early, then early stopping will lock in bad actions because the stopping rule trusts a misleading score.

items.b: Hidden reasoning is harder to inspect.
items.html: When a failure happens, it can be harder to diagnose than a visible reasoning chain because the internal path is not written out for direct inspection.
If the reward overemphasizes speed, the model may stop too soon because acting early becomes more attractive than finishing careful reasoning on hard scenes.
The method works when the confidence score is calibrated and the reward balances success with speed, because then early stopping saves time without sacrificing control.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small embodied control task, such as moving to one of several visible targets under language instructions. Compare a model that always writes full reasoning against one that keeps reasoning internal and uses an early-stop threshold.

Record task success and average internal reasoning length. The demo should show that easy scenes terminate earlier while hard scenes still use more internal steps, because the method's promise is adaptive computation rather than one fixed budget.
demo.closing: A convincing demo must show faster acting without a collapse in task success, because the paper's main claim is that some reasoning can be skipped safely.
